analysis.title: SOXxed
key_insights: The SOX index was down 10% at the time of writing. The major trend line has broken, the 200-day moving average is far above current levels, and SOX is at its most oversold level since the bull market began.
Semis have underperformed the broader market by more than 15 percentage points over the past five sessions, the worst relative performance since 2002 (GS/Bloomberg data).
Semiconductor volatility (VXSMH) is near its yearly highs at about 64, which implies daily moves of roughly 4%.
The October divergence between KOSPI VIX and VXSMH has closed. Korea had priced in panic while US semiconductors stayed calm, and US semis have now caught down.
The Market Ear describes the technical picture as awful but says the extremes have the contrarian side of the desk considering 'dipping a few toes into the water'.

SOXL is back to April levels while SOX remains well above its April levels. The note attributes this to leveraged ETF daily resets and volatility drag, and says these products need to be understood before trading.
The Market Ear has long viewed KOSPI as a leading global AI market. SOX has caught down to the Korean selloff and the relative-performance 'arb' has largely closed.

sector_views.rationale: The technical picture is described as awful with SOX at its most oversold since the bull market began. The note says it is starting to consider dipping a few toes in as a contrarian, without making a firm call.

Leveraged ETFs such as SOXL suffer from daily resets and volatility drag, which can produce large losses even when the underlying index is well above prior levels.

The KOSPI VIX vs VXSMH divergence flagged in October has closed. Those who played the long semis vol trade are told it is time to 'say thank you and move on'.
SOX is at its most oversold levels since the bull market began, and semis lag the broader market by more than 15 percentage points over five sessions, the worst relative performance since 2002.
SOXL has fallen back to April levels while SOX is well above April levels, a result of daily resets and volatility drag in leveraged ETFs.
